ratings_why.fun: Building light for a Full Moon spike and choosing how to spend the reset is a good draft, but the board can't grow for good, so it lacks the late-game pile-up.
ratings_why.distinct: What earns 8 over 7: every buff has a shelf life on a Moon that both players can see, so each buy is a timing question. No tribe today and no generic tribe works like that, and the Jacks who keep what they're given are a loophole you can read from the card frame.

verdict_why: Mostly reads cleanly now; The Hare in the Moon needs one line saying when its New Moon gift lands, or players will think it is wasted.

points.text: The Hare in the Moon triggers on a phase change, but it isn't a 'New Moon:' effect, so the card doesn't say whether its +3/+3 lands before the light goes out (wasted) or after. Say it resolves after the light goes out.

Sister Silverpenny is the one card you can't take in at a glance. Move the change-back timing into the ruling and keep the card to 'Full Moon: become a copy of your biggest unit that isn't a Hare, until the New Moon.'

The moon and the coven come through in play, but the boxing ring barely does. A jill that reacts to the enemy across, or to being attacked first, would make the March boxing a mechanic as well as a name.
Add 'New 0' to Giddy Jill's list so the dark turn reads as clearly as the other three.

standouts.why: Chalk-Cutter is one short line that turns the Full Moon into a seating puzzle.
Old Wat is the folklore joke and the rules loophole at once: the jack thrown out of the ring keeps what the jills lose.
Hare of the Three Ears makes the three-hares disc a mechanic: three units sharing one pool of light.

weakest.why: Sister Silverpenny is long, and what she becomes depends on cards from outside the tribe.
Charm-Pedlar asks for counting in tens and a cap, and pays little before the light gets big.
March Madcap is a generic pass-on-death card with little hare in it.

flags.note: Its order against the light going out at a New Moon isn't stated.
Golden Dame Waxwell with golden Chalk-Cutters multiplies light many times over in one Full Moon; capped by the reset, but worth the owner's eye.
Ringside Bookie with Moon-Caller is a buy, buff, sell loop for gold; the designer flagged it too.
